cases.name: one-arrangement
cases.about: COMP 3607 with its lectures split: every group has a single sitting, so there is nothing to choose.

cases.name: comp-year-two-three
cases.about: The four-course computing load from the spec, about 240 arrangements.

cases.name: comp-year-two-three-pinned-lecture
cases.about: comp-year-two-three with the COMP 2611 Wednesday 13:00 lecture pinned: the best week without the pin uses the Tuesday lecture, so the answer is worse.

cases.name: comp-year-two-three-with-foun
cases.about: The same four courses plus FOUN 1101, whose lectures run in week 1 only.

cases.name: first-year-large
cases.about: The largest load the brute force is asked to try, a little over three million arrangements.

cases.name: agbu-weeks-differ
cases.about: AGBU 1005 lectures and tutorials share hours but not weeks, so they never clash.

cases.name: agbu-with-biol
cases.about: AGBU 1005 beside BIOL 2061, whose classes run every week.

cases.name: split-lecture
cases.about: COMP 1601 with its lectures split into one group per time, two of which are one choice because they overlap.

cases.name: unavoidable-clash
cases.about: With COMP 1601 lectures split, its only Wednesday 12:00 lecture overlaps the only COMP 3613 lecture, Wednesday 11:00 to 13:00.

cases.name: pinned-extra-sitting
cases.about: A second COMP 2601 tutorial the student pinned: it is fixed, and the tutorial group stays loose without it.

cases.name: biol-alternate-weeks
cases.about: BIOL 1262 runs in even weeks only, beside CHEM 2470 and COMP 3613 which run every week.

cases.name: psychology-and-foundation
cases.about: Large tutorial menus: PSYC 1001, FOUN 1101 and WW101.

cases.name: sciences-mixed
cases.about: An ordinary three-course load across biology, chemistry and psychology.

cases.name: paper-two-by-two
cases.about: Small enough to work on paper: two groups of two, one pair clashes, and the front has two entries.

cases.name: paper-forced-clash
cases.about: Small enough to work on paper: every sitting clashes with the fixed class in some week, so the best week still has one clash.

cases.name: gap-thirty-minutes
cases.about: A 30-minute gap does not end a run, so the Tuesday sitting makes one run of 150 minutes.

cases.name: gap-sixty-minutes
cases.about: A 60-minute gap ends a run, so the Tuesday sitting makes two runs of 60 minutes on one day.

cases.name: uploaded-no-weeks
cases.about: An uploaded PDF gives no weeks: every event is in one undated week, and every overlap is a clash.

cases.name: uploaded-beside-dated
cases.about: An event with no weeks is present in every week another event names, so it meets a week-5 class.
